partners.mechanism_chain: TRPM6 (HGNC:12180) —DISRUPTS→ intestinal magnesium absorption (GO:0006817); intestinal magnesium absorption (GO:0006817) —DECREASES→ Magnesium ions (CHEBI:18077); Magnesium ions (CHEBI:18077) —LEADS_TO→ intestinal hypomagnesemia (HP:0002143); TRPC6 (HGNC:12175) —DISRUPTS→ podocyte ion transport (GO:0006817); podocyte ion transport (GO:0006817) —DISRUPTS→ glomerular filtration barrier integrity (GO:0001923); glomerular filtration barrier integrity (GO:0001923) —LEADS_TO→ focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (HP:0011232); Magnesium ions (CHEBI:18077) —DISRUPTS→ glomerular filtration barrier integrity (GO:0001923). Loss-of-function mutations in TRPM6 impair intestinal magnesium absorption, leading to hypomagnesemia. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in TRPC6 disrupt podocyte ion transport, compromising glomerular filtration barrier integrity and causing FSGS. partners.mechanism_chain: TRPM6 (HGNC:12069) —DISRUPTS→ Magnesium transport in the intestine; Magnesium transport in the intestine —LEADS_TO→ Intestinal hypomagnesemia (HP:0011379); TRPM1 (HGNC:12070) —DISRUPTS→ Phototransduction cascade; Phototransduction cascade —LEADS_TO→ Congenital stationary night blindness (HP:0011379). Loss-of-function mutations in TRPM6 disrupt magnesium transport in the intestine, leading to intestinal hypomagnesemia. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in TRPM1 disrupt the phototransduction cascade in retinal cells, leading to congenital stationary night blindness. While TRPM6 and TRPM1 are distinct genes, they are both members of the Transient Receptor Potential (TRP) channel superfamily, suggesting a shared mechanistic principle of ion channel dysfunction leading to tissue-specific pathologies. The convergence lies in the disruption of critical ion transport processes by homologous channel proteins.

**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3295583)

Loss-of-function mutations in both TRPM6 and TRPM3 disrupt magnesium transport and homeostasis, leading to intestinal hypomagnesemia. These same disrupted pathways, along with direct roles in neuronal function, also contribute to hypotonia, dysmorphic facies, and skeletal anomalies, indicating a shared biological basis for these distinct disease presentations.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in TRPM6 or TRPM3 exhibiting a loss-of-function phenotype that is exclusively one of the two diseases, without any overlap in the affected systems (e.g., isolated intestinal hypomagnesemia without neurological involvement, or vice versa), would challenge the proposed shared mechanistic link. _(variant: A common variant (AF > 1%) in the gnomAD database in a critical functional domain of TRPM6 or TRPM3 that is associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic basis involving TRPM6 and TRPM3 could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both intestinal hypomagnesemia and neurodevelopmental disorders, potentially through modulating ion channel function or compensating for magnesium deficiency.
